messages:
Marta (Account Exec): Heads-up — BrightApps just asked for a short, customer-friendly timeline + confirmation of any SLA credit. They want a single-paragraph summary and a clear ask for next steps. Can we draft and send today? Link to current draft: https://redwood.docs/drafts/brightapps-rfc (please don't edit that file directly).

Amanda (CS): Thanks Marta — I can assemble a concise note. Can someone confirm exact start/end times and whether embeddings were affected or just routing? I also need the mitigations we promised so I can list them.

Ravi (Oncall): Start: 2026-03-15 14:02 UTC — routing fallback triggered when the regional routing queue spiked. Full mitigation (fallback to secondary model variant + cache warm up) at 14:15 UTC. Service returned to normal by 14:18 UTC. No data loss.

Jordan (SRE): Confirming Ravi's timeline. Root cause: a compilation backlog on the routing host group after a sudden burst of long-context requests from a single customer org; that caused controller backpressure and delayed new routing decisions. Affected requests were routed to slower fallback paths for ~13 minutes. Embeddings service was not impacted; only customer-facing text-generation routes in eu-west-1 that use the new routing plugin.

IncidentBot: Incident INCIDENT-2026-03-15-ROUTINGFALLBACK created at 2026-03-15T14:03Z. Severity: P2. Linked postmortem: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-03-15.

BrightApps - Ops: Thanks for the quick updates. The customer is mainly worried about SLA credits and whether we will prevent this class of issue from repeating. They appreciate a short timeline + one-sentence root cause + actions.

Amanda (CS): Draft for customer (single-paragraph): "On 15 Mar 2026 at ~14:02 UTC we observed elevated routing latency in eu-west-1 that caused a subset of text-generation requests to be served by fallback paths for about 13 minutes. The issue was triggered by a compilation backlog that built up after an unusual burst of long-context requests; embeddings and other regions were not affected. We mitigated the issue by routing traffic to verified secondary model variants and warming KV caches, and service normalized by 14:18 UTC. We will issue an SLA credit for the affected window and implement controller-side rate damping + a compilation backlog alert to reduce recurrence. Please let us know if you'd like a brief call to review the timeline."

Marta (Account Exec): That reads well. Can we be explicit about the SLA credit? BrightApps asked for a dollar estimate or percent. What's the recommended credit?

Jordan (SRE): Per our SLA calc: affected window = 16 minutes (we're conservative: 14:02–14:18 inclusive) for their reserved Dedicated capacity plan. Their monthly committed hours worth ~0.5% of monthly availability lost. Recommend offering a 0.5% credit on their next invoice + an offer for a one-off free consult to tune routing quotas.

Ravi (Oncall): Action items I can own: 1) Add a compilation backlog alert to the controller (low-severity monitor) — ETA 48h. 2) Add a short-circuit check to fallback earlier when backlog > threshold — ETA 72h (will need a small runtime change). 3) Post the technical postmortem link in status page — done (I'll update with exact times).

Amanda (CS): I'll finalize the customer note with the recommended 0.5% credit and the offer for a consult. Draft message to send (for review):

---
Hi BrightApps team — thanks again for your patience. On 15 Mar 2026 at approximately 14:02 UTC, we experienced elevated routing latency in eu-west-1 that caused a portion of text-generation traffic to be served via fallback paths for roughly 13 minutes. The root cause was a compilation backlog that formed after an unusual burst of long-context requests from a single tenant; embeddings and other regions were unaffected. We mitigated the issue by routing traffic to verified secondary model variants and warming caches; normal service resumed by 14:18 UTC. We will apply a 0.5% credit to your next invoice for the impacted window and will schedule a short consult to review routing quotas. As preventative actions, we are (a) adding a controller compilation-backlog alert, (b) implementing a faster fallback short-circuit, and (c) reviewing quota safeguards for long-context requests. Please let us know if you'd like a quick call to walk through the timeline.

Thanks,
Amanda and the Redwood Incident Team
---

Marta (Account Exec): Approve to send. I can take the call if customer requests. Amanda, please send and cc me.

Jordan (SRE): For the internal postmortem section, I'll add a short timeline snippet and the proposed code change PR reference: PR #4821 (routing: fallback short-circuit) and monitor ticket MON-789.

BrightApps - Ops: That looks good to us. We'll wait for the note and the invoice credit. Appreciate the consult offer.

Ravi (Oncall): Closing loop: I updated the incident page with the final timestamps and linked PR/monitor tickets. Leaving the oncall follow-up checklist items assigned to me for the next two business days.

Amanda (CS): Sent to customer and cc'd Marta. Copy of sent message: https://redwood.outbound/brightapps-2026-03-15. Will follow up in 48h to schedule the consult.

Marta (Account Exec): Thanks team — great coordination. Amanda, please open a quick calendar poll for the consult and add Jordan if they want to join the technical portion. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (SRE): I'll join the consult. Also filing a retro note to review long-context quota defaults.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT-2026-03-15 status changed to RESOLVED at 2026-03-15T15:00Z."
